purpose: Insert is the left-sidebar panel a user opens to put a new element, block, shipped component or saved component onto the current page — the editor's create door.
task: Drag an element row from Insert onto the canvas
finding: Dragging an element out of Insert can land nothing on the page and still report success. The drop dispatcher pre-reads every DataTransfer channel synchronously (its own header explains why: 'a single microtask boundary (e.g. await) zeros it out'), then hands `payloads` to five handlers — and only handleCatalogDrop reads it. handleBlockDrop, the terminal branch that every Insert-panel drag lands in, takes only (e, ctx) and re-reads `e.dataTransfer.getData("block")` itself. It runs AFTER `await handleComponentDrop(...)`, which is an async function, so the read happens past the microtask boundary the file warns about and returns "" in a real browser. handleBlockDrop then returns false — and the dispatcher's else-branch sets `dropSucceeded = true` unconditionally, so DragManager is told the drop worked, no error toast fires, and the user sees a drag that did nothing with no explanation.
evidence: useDropExecution.ts:183-195 (pre-snapshot + the comment), :293 (await handleComponentDrop), :295 (handleCatalogDrop IS given payloads), :302-303 (handleBlockDrop called with a payloads arg its signature drops, then dropSucceeded=true regardless); dropOperations.tsx:238 (handleComponentDrop is `export async function`), :375-377 (handleBlockDrop signature + direct getData). Not caught by tests because the mock DataTransfer never empties: __tests__/dropOperations.test.ts:168-169 `getData: (type) => payloads[type] ?? ""`. Searched: 'getData', 'dataTransfer', 'payloads', 'DropPayloads', 'blockData'.
fix: The drag path must be as reliable as the click path, and a drop that places nothing must say so. Give handleBlockDrop the pre-read payload the dispatcher already captured, and make dropSucceeded reflect what the handler returned so a no-op drop raises the same 'couldn't place that' message a refused drop does.

purpose: Insert is the left-sidebar panel a user opens to put a new element, block, shipped component or saved component onto the current page — the editor's create door.
task: Add a child element from the canvas selection toolbar
finding: The canvas selection toolbar's + opens a picker that tells the user an element was added when nothing was. The picker's own click handler fires a success toast ('Added Button to canvas') BEFORE it calls through to the inserter; the inserter then checks nesting, and on failure calls devLogger and onClose() — no message, no element. Same for 'target element not found' and 'block config not found'. The modal disappears, a green success toast is on screen, and the canvas is unchanged.
evidence: useElementsState.ts:151-161 — trackSidebar then `addToast({description: \`Added ${block.label} to canvas\`, tone:"success"})` then `onBlockClick?.(block)`; BlockPickerModal.tsx:41-63 (two silent devLogger+onClose returns), :91-100 (`if (!canNestElement(...)) { devLogger...; onClose(); return; }`). Searched: 'addToast', 'devLogger', 'canNestElement', 'onClose'.
fix: Move the success signal after the insert actually returns an id, and give every refusal the same contextual message the sidebar path already writes ('Can't add Button — heading doesn't allow it. Try selecting a container first.'). Keep the modal open on refusal so the user can pick something else.

purpose: Insert is the left-sidebar panel a user opens to put a new element, block, shipped component or saved component onto the current page — the editor's create door.
task: Add an element to the page
finding: There are three different ways to add an element and they disagree about what the catalog even is. (1) The sidebar Insert panel groups by SOURCE — ELEMENTS 53 rows, BLOCKS 50 cards, COMPONENTS 14 rows, MINE n — off a hand-written catalog. (2) The canvas selection toolbar's + opens a modal with a completely different picker that groups by TYPE, has Most Used / Recents / Favourites and per-element descriptions, and reads the 64-entry block registry directly. (3) The canvas right-click Insert submenu offers no catalog at all — every entry inserts the same unnamed placeholder div. A user who learns one map cannot use the others.
evidence: BuildTab.tsx:214-229 + catalog/groups.ts:48-55 (source groups); ToolbarActionsSection.tsx:50-51 ('Add Element' button) -> UnifiedSelectionToolbar.tsx:186,322-327 -> BlockPickerModal.tsx:17,187 -> ElementsTab.tsx:190-226 (category accordions) + useElementsState.ts:111-121 ('Most Used' + CATEGORY_REMAP); insertActions.ts:13-19,21-59. Searched: 'ElementsTab', 'BlockPicker', 'insertSubmenu', 'onAdd', 'handleQuickAdd'.
fix: Pick one catalog and one picker and route all three entry points at it. The toolbar + and the context menu should open the same list the sidebar shows, seeded with the target element as the insertion context, rather than each shipping its own taxonomy.

purpose: Insert is the left-sidebar panel a user opens to put a new element, block, shipped component or saved component onto the current page — the editor's create door.
task: Find the element I want in Insert
finding: Every single one of the 53 ELEMENTS rows is the same registry block as something further down the same panel — 40 of them reappear as a BLOCKS card and 13 as a COMPONENTS row. A user scrolling Insert meets Card, Table, Progress, Countdown, Accordion, Tabs, Modal, Pricing, Testimonials twice, once as a 28px text row that can be dragged and once as a 136px card that cannot, sometimes under a different label. Nothing on screen says the two are the same thing.

Set-compared the 53 catalog blockIds against both lists: 40 land in BLOCKS (audio button checkbox color columns container cta date divider email file flex footer form gallery grid heading icon image input label link list lottie map-embed navbar number paragraph password radio range section select spacer submit svg textarea time video video-embed), 13 in COMPONENTS (accordion card countdown modal pricing progress slider social-icons stack switch table tabs testimonials), 0 in neither. Searched: 'blockId', 'flatCatalog', 'componentBlockDefinitions', 'getBlockDefinitions'.

}`; `preview?: string` is declared at shared/types/block.ts:25 but `grep -rn preview packages/editor/src/blocks/` returns zero hits, and the block configs carry only an `icon` path (Heading.tsx:17 `icon: "/src/assets/icons/blocks/basic/heading.svg"`) that nothing in Insert renders. purpose: Insert is the left-sidebar panel a user opens to put a new element, block, shipped component or saved component onto the current page — the editor's create door.
task: Drag something from Insert onto a specific spot on the canvas
finding: Only 53 of the panel's ~117 offerings can be dragged. The ELEMENTS rows pass `draggable`; the BLOCKS cards, the COMPONENTS rows and the MINE rows do not, so they can only be clicked and dropped wherever smart placement decides. That is exactly backwards from the user's need: a bare Heading is easy to place afterwards, a 12-row Pricing block or a saved component is the thing you most want to aim. The panel's own purpose line is honest about it ('Drag elements onto the canvas instead'), but nothing on a BLOCKS card says why it will not pick up.
evidence: GroupSection.tsx:181-193 (elements Row gets `draggable` at :189 and an onDragStart at :190), :206-213 (components rows: no draggable, no onDragStart), :217-224 (mine rows: same), :234-262 (blocks cards: role=button + onClick + onKeyDown only). BuildTab.tsx:187-193 (the purpose line, and its comment at :180-183 explaining the narrowing). Searched: 'draggable', 'onDragStart', 'dataTransfer.setData'.
fix: Make every insertable thing draggable, or make nothing draggable and give click-insert a visible target preview. A panel where the drag affordance depends on which group a row is in cannot be learned.

purpose: Insert is the left-sidebar panel a user opens to put a new element, block, shipped component or saved component onto the current page — the editor's create door.

finding: The onboarding checklist tells the user to 'Drop a ready-made section — hero, features, footer — onto the canvas' and its button opens the Insert panel. purpose: Insert is the left-sidebar panel a user opens to put a new element, block, shipped component or saved component onto the current page — the editor's create door.
task: Come back to the group I was browsing
finding: Which groups are open is component-local state with no persistence, and TabRouter mounts one tab at a time, so the panel unmounts the moment the user clicks any other rail tool. Leaving Insert to look at Layers and coming back re-collapses BLOCKS/COMPONENTS/MINE, re-expands ELEMENTS and resets the scroll to the top of the 53 rows. Meanwhile the hook underneath still saves an `openCats` set to sessionStorage every render — for the category model this panel stopped rendering.
evidence: BuildTab.tsx:49-51 `React.useState(() => new Set<InsertGroupId>(["elements"]))` — no read from storage, no write; TabRouter.tsx:124-126 (switch returns one tab, so BuildTab unmounts on tab change); useBuildTab.ts:107-117 + :136-138 (openCats read/written to STORAGE_KEYS.BUILD_OPEN_CATS) with no consumer — BuildTab destructures none of `openCats`/`toggleCat`. Searched: 'openGroups', 'openCats', 'BUILD_OPEN_CATS', 'sessionSaveSet'.
fix: Persist which groups are open (and the scroll offset) per session, keyed the way the dead openCats already is. A user assembling a page returns to Insert dozens of times per sitting.

purpose: Insert is the left-sidebar panel a user opens to put a new element, block, shipped component or saved component onto the current page — the editor's create door.
task: Work out which of 53 elements is the one I need
finding: Every catalog entry carries a written one-line description ('Swipeable image or content carousel', 'Numeric input with steppers'), and the user can never read one. The row only passes the description into a tooltip when the entry is marked disabled — and no entry is. The result is 53 near-identical text rows with a 14px glyph and a bare noun, so a user looking for a pricing table cannot tell whether to use Table, Grid, Card or Pricing, and the panel holds the answer in a field it never shows.

The rival picker DOES show a description per element (ElementCard.tsx:33,64). Searched: 'description', 'disabledReason', 'Tooltip', 'title='.

purpose: Insert is the left-sidebar panel a user opens to put a new element, block, shipped component or saved component onto the current page — the editor's create door.

At the same time 11 real registry blocks have no element row at all (hero, features, text, row, column, columns3, contact-form, product-card, product-grid, product-detail, cart-button), so they are absent from ELEMENTS with no marker saying where they went. purpose: Insert is the left-sidebar panel a user opens to put a new element, block, shipped component or saved component onto the current page — the editor's create door.
task: Find my own saved component from Insert
finding: Search in Insert covers elements, shipped blocks and shipped components — but never MINE, the user's own saved components. The search call is passed the catalog, blockRows and componentRows and nothing else, so typing the name of a component you saved yourself returns "Nothing matches 'x'" while that component is sitting in a group on the same screen. purpose: Insert is the left-sidebar panel a user opens to put a new element, block, shipped component or saved component onto the current page — the editor's create door.
task: Get back to the full list after a search
finding: There is no way to clear the search that is visible while results exist. The field draws no clear (x) affordance by design; Escape only clears while focus is still inside the search wrapper, because the handler is bound to that div — tab down into the results and Escape does nothing; and the 'Clear search' link only renders in the zero-results state. So the common case — a search that matched three things, none of them right — leaves the user with no button to press to see the panel again.

Searched: 'Clear search', 'onClearSearch', 'Escape', 'kbdHint', 'clearable'.
fix: Give the field a clear control whenever it has text, or move Escape-to-clear to the panel root so it works from anywhere in Insert.

purpose: Insert is the left-sidebar panel a user opens to put a new element, block, shipped component or saved component onto the current page — the editor's create door.
task: Judge whether my search worked

'button' matches across elements, blocks and components; the user cannot see how many hits there are, where one source ends and the next begins, or whether the list is scrolled. purpose: Insert is the left-sidebar panel a user opens to put a new element, block, shipped component or saved component onto the current page — the editor's create door.
task: Learn how to use the Insert panel

The strip renders only '💡 Tip 1/4 ‹ › x' — the tip body exists but is passed as a `title` attribute on the whole strip, so it only surfaces on a slow hover over the band. Pressing 'next' therefore changes a number and nothing else. purpose: Insert is the left-sidebar panel a user opens to put a new element, block, shipped component or saved component onto the current page — the editor's create door.
task: Bring the tips back after dismissing them

The flag is written to localStorage, not session storage, so it survives every reload; and the Insert panel has no Help button, because the header only renders one when an onHelpClick is supplied and the sidebar's commonTabProps does not include that key at all. purpose: Insert is the left-sidebar panel a user opens to put a new element, block, shipped component or saved component onto the current page — the editor's create door.
task: Understand a notice the panel shows me
finding: Returning users with old Quick Picks get a callout at the top of Insert saying 'Quick Picks removed. Browse and drag elements directly from categories below.' There are no categories below — there are four source groups — and only one of those groups can be dragged. The callout also has no dismiss control of its own; it disappears on an 8-second timer, so a user who looks away misses it entirely and a user who reads slowly cannot stop it.

purpose: Insert is the left-sidebar panel a user opens to put a new element, block, shipped component or saved component onto the current page — the editor's create door.
task: Add an image to the page
finding: Clicking Image, Video, Audio, Icon, SVG or Lottie in Insert silently replaces the panel you are in: the insert handler emits a tab switch to Media and then a needs-asset event, so the Insert panel is gone and the Media library is open with a filter applied. If the user then picks an asset, Media switches back to Insert — the round trip closes. If the user does anything else (closes the picker, clicks Cancel, changes their mind), nothing routes them back: they are left in Media, with an empty media element already selected on the canvas, and the only way back to Insert is to find the rail again.
evidence: useBlockInsertion.ts:144-153 (mediaTypes set; `composer.emit("ui:switch-tab",{tab:"assets"})` then a 100ms-delayed `element:needs-asset`), and its comment at :129-143 admitting the timing hack; useMediaState.ts:133-143 (needsAssetHandler sets selectionContext + switches to assets), :243 (`ui:switch-tab {tab:"add"}` only on the APPLY branch); MediaTab.tsx:378 `onCancelSelection={() => state.setSelectionContext(null)}` — clears the context, emits no tab switch. Searched: 'ui:switch-tab', 'element:needs-asset', 'ELEMENT_NEEDS_ASSET', 'selectionContext', 'onCancelSelection'.
fix: Cancelling the asset pick should return to Insert the same way applying one does, and should offer to remove the empty element it left behind. Better still, show the picker over the canvas instead of hijacking the left panel.

purpose: Insert is the left-sidebar panel a user opens to put a new element, block, shipped component or saved component onto the current page — the editor's create door.
task: Add an image by dragging it in from Insert
finding: The same Image row behaves differently depending on whether you click it or drag it. Click routes through the shell hook, which detects an empty media element and opens the Media picker for you. Drag routes through the canvas drop handler, which has no such branch — it inserts an image element with no src, selects it, and stops. The user gets a broken-image placeholder and no indication that an asset is what is missing, from the very affordance the panel tells them to prefer ('Drag elements onto the canvas instead').
evidence: useBlockInsertion.ts:144-153 (the needs-asset branch, click path only); dropOperations.tsx:375-527 (handleBlockDrop — no mediaTypes check, no element:needs-asset emit); a full grep for 'element:needs-asset' / ELEMENT_NEEDS_ASSET finds emitters only at useBlockInsertion.ts:148 and listeners at useMediaState.ts:144 — nothing in the drag path; blocks/Media/Image.tsx:18-19 confirms the block ships with no src on purpose and relies on that event. Searched: 'element:needs-asset', 'ELEMENT_NEEDS_ASSET', 'mediaTypes', 'needsAsset'.
fix: Fire the same needs-asset handoff from the drop path, so click and drag of a media element reach the same next step.

purpose: Insert is the left-sidebar panel a user opens to put a new element, block, shipped component or saved component onto the current page — the editor's create door.
task: See where an element will land before I let go
finding: While dragging from Insert the canvas draws a valid/invalid drop indicator that is not computed for the thing being dragged. During dragover the browser will not release the payload, so the validator only sees that a 'block' MIME exists and asks whether a generic CONTAINER could nest in the hovered target — not whether a Submit, a Column or a Table could. A green line therefore promises a placement the drop then refuses with a 'Cannot place X inside Y' warning. The check is narrowed further by a guard that skips it entirely whenever the target has a parent, which is nearly always.
evidence: dragCalculations.ts:145-156 — `if (dataTransferTypes.includes("block")) { … canNestElement("container", targetType) … if (!targetCanContainChildren && position === "inside") { const hasParent = …; if (!hasParent) return {isValid:false} } }`; useDropTargetResolver.ts:136-148 (feeds that verdict to showInvalidTarget and to composer.canvas.drag.move); dropOperations.tsx:481-489 (the real per-type check, and the NESTING_FORBIDDEN message, only at drop time). Searched: 'validateDropOperation', 'dataTransferTypes', 'NESTING_FORBIDDEN', 'showInvalidTarget'.
fix: Put the dragged element's type where the dragover handler can read it — a module-level 'drag in progress' record set on dragstart — so the indicator answers the same question the drop will.

purpose: Insert is the left-sidebar panel a user opens to put a new element, block, shipped component or saved component onto the current page — the editor's create door.
task: Know that my insert worked
finding: The two insert paths have opposite feedback contracts. A click from Insert raises a visible 'Inserted: Heading' toast. A drag from Insert raises nothing visible at all — the drop success handler deliberately routes the same sentence into a visually-hidden live region and only toasts when the operation is still in flight. Both decisions are defensible on their own; together they mean the user is taught that inserting produces a toast, and then the affordance the panel recommends produces silence.
evidence: useBlockInsertion.ts:155 `addToast({description: \`Inserted: ${block.label}\`, tone:"success", duration:2000})`; Canvas.tsx:149-162 handleDropSuccess — `announce(...)` only, `addToast` only when `success.pending`, with the reasoning at :127-137 ('Every successful drop raised a toast … the visual noise goes'). Searched: 'addToast', 'onDropSuccess', 'announce', 'Inserted:'.
fix: Choose one. If the canvas flash plus auto-selection is enough signal for a drop, it is enough for a click too; drop the click toast and keep the live-region announcement for both.

purpose: Insert is the left-sidebar panel a user opens to put a new element, block, shipped component or saved component onto the current page — the editor's create door.
task: See the element I just inserted
finding: Clicking a row inserts at the end of the page when nothing is selected, and nothing scrolls the canvas there. On a page longer than the viewport the user gets a two-second toast and no visible change — the new element, its success flash and its selection ring are all below the fold. The editor has the code to move the viewport (zoom-to-selection, deep-link scrollIntoView, the Layers panel's own scroll) and no insert path calls it.
evidence: useBlockInsertion.ts:74-75 (parent/index default to the root's end), :118-127 (select + a flash that queries the DOM but never scrolls); dropOperations.tsx:494-514 (same, for drops). A repo-wide grep for 'scrollIntoView' finds it in PageCommandPalette, CommandPalette x2, useDeepLink.ts:44, layers/index.tsx:186 and Canvas.tsx:349 (handleZoomToSelection, a user-invoked command) — none on an insert path. Searched: 'scrollIntoView', 'scrollTo', 'animateDropSuccess', 'zoomToSelection'.
fix: Scroll the newly inserted element into view before flashing it, on every insert path.

purpose: Insert is the left-sidebar panel a user opens to put a new element, block, shipped component or saved component onto the current page — the editor's create door.
task: Add something inside a component instance or a locked container
finding: The product disagrees with itself about inserting into a component instance. The canvas context menu hides 'Insert inside' for an instance, with a comment saying structural inserts there are discarded by the next instance sync. The Insert panel and the canvas drop path have no such guard — smart placement will happily walk into the selected instance, insert, select the new element and toast success, and the work is thrown away on the next sync with nothing said. Locked elements are unguarded on every path: nothing in the insert chain consults isLocked, only nesting rules.
evidence: insertActions.ts:68-69 and :89-90 `isVisible: ctx => ctx.element.canHaveChildren() && !ctx.element.isLocked() && !ctx.element.isComponentInstance?.()` with the comment at :65-67 ('Structural inserts inside an instance subtree are discarded by the next syncInstance'); useBlockInsertion.ts:77-115 (walks parents on canNestElement alone) and dropOperations.tsx:409-489 (same) — neither calls isLocked or isComponentInstance; a repo-wide grep for 'isComponentInstance' finds guards only in insertActions.ts, useCanvasKeyboard.ts:145, LayerTreeItem.tsx and the engine, and `grep isLocked` over blocks/ + the two insert paths returns nothing. Searched: 'isComponentInstance', 'isLocked', 'canNestElement', 'syncInstance'.
fix: Apply the context menu's rule everywhere: refuse the insert with the reason ('Detach this instance first'), or place the element as a sibling outside the instance. Same for locked containers.

purpose: Insert is the left-sidebar panel a user opens to put a new element, block, shipped component or saved component onto the current page — the editor's create door.
finding: PURPOSE: Insert is the editor's create door — the left-sidebar panel (rail 'Insert', shortcut A, tab id 'add') where a user gets a new element, a shipped block, a shipped component or one of their own saved components onto the current page. PRIMARY TASKS: (1) find the right thing among ~117 offerings, by scanning four collapsible source groups or by searching across three of them; (2) place it — click for smart placement relative to the selection, or drag an ELEMENTS row onto a specific spot; (3) paste raw HTML through the pinned '⌥ Paste HTML…' row. ENTRY POINTS, all verified: the rail Insert button and shortcut A (tabsConfig.ts:74-85, useSidebarKeyboard.ts:34-47); the command palette's 'Open Insert panel' (CommandPalette.tsx:53-56); the empty-canvas CTA's 'Start blank', which emits ui:switch-tab {tab:'add'} (Canvas.tsx:737-746); the onboarding checklist step 'Insert a section' (onboardingSteps.ts:57-65); and a return trip from Media after an asset is applied (useMediaState.ts:243). EXIT POINTS: the header ✕ (drawer toggle) and expand; switching rail tools; and one involuntary exit — inserting any media element force-switches the panel to Media (useBlockInsertion.ts:144-153), whose cancel path does not bring you back. HANDS OFF TO: the canvas and Inspector (every insert path selects the new element, and the Inspector is always mounted, so the right panel follows automatically — StudioPanels.tsx:493-514); Media (the needs-asset handoff); the CMS collection-setup modal (product blocks, useComposerInit.ts:735-763); Components/MINE (instantiate). RECEIVES FROM: the block registry (64 definitions, blockRegistry.ts:100-202) and a separate hand-written 53-entry element catalog; the composer's component registry for MINE; the selection, which decides where a click lands. RIVALS: two other insert surfaces with different catalogs and different rules — the canvas selection toolbar's + (BlockPickerModal -> ElementsTab, type-grouped, with favourites/recents/descriptions) and the right-click Insert submenu (placeholder divs, no catalog) — plus a fourth, unreachable implementation (handleQuickAdd). THE SHAPE OF THE PROBLEM: the panel's information architecture shows the same 53 things twice under different headers with different affordances; its one picture-based group has no pictures; the descriptions, favourites, recents and 'Soon' states it already contains are all built and unrendered; and its two placement methods (click, drag) differ in feedback, in media handling and in reliability.
